To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a wave of Ca(2+) release crosses the egg cytoplams, that this wave is due to the progressive release of Ca(2+), that the progressive release of C(2+) is due to the diffusion of InsP(3), that InsP(3) production is due to Ca(2+) entry through the sperm receptor, and that Ca(2+) stimulates InsP(3)-induced Ca(2+)release from a store within egg cytoplasm.
a wave of InsP3 release from an internal egg store is the most likely mechanism to account for the propagation of the calcium release wave at fertilization in sea urchins.
a wave of InsP3-induced Ca2+ release propagates from the site of sperm entry to the animal pole in sea urchins, and that this wave can account for the propagation of the Ca2+ wave.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of activation of the sea urchin egg.
the role of calcium and the inositol phosphates in the fertilization of the sea urchin egg.
the role of the inositol trphosphate/calcium second messenger system in the activation of sea urchin fertilization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the wave of calcium released at fertilization is the result of the production of inositols by the action of the sperm on the egg and that the inositols diffuse through the cytoplasm and induce the release of calcium from an internal store.
the fertilization wave is a result of a calcium-InsP3 cycle that is initiated at the point of fertilization and diffuses across the egg cytosol with the velocity of 5-10 microns/sec.

the wave of calcium released at fertilization in sea urchins is due to the production and diffusion through the egg of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate, which in turn is due to a wave of calcium released from an internal store.

the activation wave in sea uredin is the result of the progressive production of InsP, which in turn causes the progressive release of Ca.

InsP3, not calcium, diffuses through the sea urchin egg cytoplasm and that calcium-stimulation of InsP3 synthesis and InsP3 induced release of calcium from an internal store accounts for the progressive release and propagation of calcium across the egg.
the activation wave is due to the diffusion of InsP3 across the egg cytosol.
The main takeaway from our work is that
InsP3 is a second messenger that diffuses through the cytoplasm of the sea urchin egg.
the fertilization wave is due to the progressive release of InsP3 from an internal store, which then stimulates the release of calcium from another internal store.
calcium release at fertilization is due to the activation of InsP3 receptors, and that InsP3 can diffuse through the cytosol.
